DISCUSSION
Generators perform the opposite function of motors.........
A mechanical input is used to generate an electrical output.
Generators are often used where electricity is not available.
The mechanical input to the generator can be supplied by a number of different sources.
Gas and diesel engines are used to produce mechanical input power to a generator.
Electric motors are also used to produce mechanical input power to a generator.
As an electronics technician, you will primarily encounter the motor generator.
There are two types of generators: AC and DC..............
The AC generator produces AC or alternating current........
The DC generator produces DC or direct current.
In this lesson, DC generators will be discussed.
DC Generators are nearly identical to DC Motors............
The DC Generator's theory of operation is similar to a DC Motor's.
Recall, for a DC motor, if a current carrying conductor is placed in a magnetic field, motion of the conductor results.
By the same theory, if a conductor is moved through a magnetic field, current is induced in the moving conductor.
If a load (resistance) is attached to the conductor, current will flow.
This phenomenon is similar to the effects that are necessary for inductive reactance or transformer action.
The equation to determine the amount of induced voltage in the conductor is also the same as mutual inductance.
where; N = # of conductors series aiding)
From the equation you can see that to induce a voltage (a combination of flux), motion and a conductor are required.
In generation action, a conductor moves through a magnetic field, producing a current flow.
This current is flowing through a conductor that is in a magnetic field.
The result of this, which is motor action, produces additional torque.
From the Right Hand Rule, you will see that this torque opposes the direction of conductor motion (mechanical torque).
The counter torque is proportional to the current flowing through the conductor.
As the load current increases (P ), Counter Torque also increases. This requires more force to move the conductor through the field (P ).
If a large enough load is placed on the generator, motor action counter torque will cause the conductor to stop moving through the field and generator action will cease.

The construction of DC generators is almost identical to DC motors.
Both the DC motor and generator use stators, rotors, and commutators.
In a DC motor, current is sent to the rotor windings, causing a motor output of the shaft.
In a DC generator, the rotor is driven, causing a current from the rotor windings.
The amount of induced voltage across the rotor windings depends on the position of the rotor with respect to the field.

As in DC motors, DC generators use permanent or electromagnets to produce the field or stator flux.
In permanent magnet DC generators, the field magnetic flux is always present.
When the rotor is rotated, a DC Voltage output occurs.
In electromagnet DC generators, there are two types of machines.
A Separately Excited generator uses an external source to supply current to the field or stator windings.
A separately excited DC generator uses a shunt field only.
A Self Excited generator does not use an external voltage source to produce the field or stator magnetic flux.
The voltage produced in the armature or rotor supplies the field or stator current.
The rotor current induces field winding voltage which induces rotor current. This is possible due to residual magnetism.
With no rotor rotation, there is no rotor current or power to the field windings.
When a rotating force is applied to the rotor, the rotor begins to cut the very weak flux field produced by a residual magnetism.
The small E voltage is also applied to the field windings, increasing the flux - increasing E as RPM increases.
A higher E produces a larger flux field, which produces a higher E as RPM increases.
The process continues until equilibrium occurs.
